Theologically, it reminds us that God uses human relationships to fortify our trust in Him.

This verb means 'to trust' or 'to rely on'. It expresses a deep assurance and dependence on God. In this verse, Jonathan helps David renew his trust in God, emphasizing the importance of active faith in trials. Spiritually, it reminds us that our trust in God must be regularly renewed, especially in times of crisis.

This word means 'hand', but it is often used symbolically to denote power, authority, or action. In the context of this passage, Jonathan's hand reaches out to David to encourage him, illustrating how human actions can be instruments of divine grace. It teaches us that we have a role to play in the lives of others to help them see God's hand in their struggles.

16.epoque: This passage takes place during the time of the Israelite monarchy, when Saul, the king, was pursuing David out of jealousy and fear of losing his throne.
16.passage: In this chapter, David finds himself in a desperate situation, fleeing from Saul. Jonathan, despite his familial ties to Saul, chooses to support David, demonstrating the depth of their friendship and loyalty to God's plan.
16.culture: In the Israelite culture of the time, friendship and loyalty were fundamental values. Jonathan represents the ideal of the faithful friend who sets aside his own interests to support a friend in need.
16.interpretation: This verse illustrates the importance of mutual encouragement in faith. By strengthening David, Jonathan demonstrates that trust in God can be reinforced through human relationships, highlighting the role of the Church in the lives of believers.
16.commentaire: This passage reminds us that even in the darkest moments, God can send friends to encourage and strengthen our faith. Like Jonathan, we are called to be instruments of support for those going through trials. Let us cultivate relationships that strengthen our trust in God and remember that our faith is often renewed through the love and support of others.

mots.sens: This word means 'to be evil' or 'to do harm'. In the context of this verse, it evokes the threat that Saul poses to David. The root of this word is related to harmful actions, highlighting the tension between David and Saul. Spiritually, it reminds us that even in difficult situations, God protects those who are faithful to Him.

This term means 'to reign' or 'to govern'. It is often used to denote authority and power, especially in the context of royalty. David's promise to reign over Israel is both a declaration of faith and a reminder of God's sovereignty in establishing leaders. It emphasizes the idea that God has a plan for every believer, even in times of uncertainty.

This word means 'hand' and symbolizes power, authority, and action. In this verse, 'the hand of Saul' represents the direct threat against David, but also the divine protection surrounding him. Theologically, it reminds us that God's hand is always present to support and defend those who are in His purpose.

17.epoque: This passage takes place during the time of the monarchy in Israel, during Saul's reign, when David is fleeing due to Saul's jealousy. It is a period of transition and conflict within the people of Israel.
17.passage: In this chapter, David is in danger, pursued by Saul. Jonathan, Saul's son and David's friend, brings him a message of encouragement and support, affirming that David will be the future king of Israel.
17.culture: At this time, familial loyalty and alliances were crucial. Jonathan, despite his position as the king's son, chooses to support his friend David, illustrating the importance of friendship and loyalty beyond familial ties.
17.interpretation: This verse shows Jonathan's trust in the divine promise concerning David. It reminds believers that even in the face of adversity, faithfulness to God and His promises is essential. Jonathan's declaration is an act of faith that reinforces the idea that God has a plan for each of us.
17.commentaire: This passage teaches us not to fear the threats that may surround us, for God is our protector. Just as Jonathan encouraged David, we are called to support our brothers and sisters in faith, reminding them of God's promises. By remaining faithful, we can be assured that God has a plan for us, even in the darkest moments.

mots.sens: This word means 'covenant' and evokes a solemn commitment between two parties. In the biblical context, it often represents a sacred relationship, marked by promises and reciprocal obligations. The root of the word emphasizes the idea of bond and fidelity, making it a central concept in the relationship between God and His people, as well as in human relationships. In this verse, the covenant between David and Jonathan symbolizes deep loyalty and mutual support in difficult times.

This name designates the Eternal, the God of Israel, and evokes His eternal and unchanging nature. In the Hebrew tradition, this name is associated with holiness, sovereignty, and promise. As the God who establishes covenants, YHWH is the guarantor of the commitments made, which gives a sacred dimension to the covenant between David and Jonathan. It underscores the divine presence in their relationships and divine support in their struggles.

This verb means 'to remain' or 'to dwell', and it implies a notion of stability and permanence. In this context, it indicates that David chooses to stay in the forest, a place of refuge and safety, despite the dangers surrounding him. It evokes trust in God for His protection and guidance, a recurring theme in David's life as he flees from Saul. Spiritually, it reminds us of the importance of finding our dwelling in God, even in times of uncertainty.

18.epoque: This passage takes place during the period of the Israelite monarchy, while David is fleeing due to Saul's jealousy, the king of Israel.
18.passage: In this chapter, David faces major challenges, but he receives support from Jonathan, his friend and Saul's son. Their covenant forms in a context of tension, but it is based on values of loyalty and faith.
18.culture: In Israelite culture, covenants were sacred commitments, often sealed by rituals and promises before God. This reflects the importance of interpersonal relationships and fidelity within the community.
18.interpretation: The covenant between David and Jonathan illustrates the depth of friendship and loyalty, even in adverse circumstances. Spiritually, it reminds us that God places people in our lives to support us in our struggles and that these relationships should be nurtured by faith and commitment.
18.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of loyalty and commitment in our relationships. Just as David and Jonathan made a covenant before the Lord, we are called to build strong relationships based on faith and mutual trust. In times of uncertainty, let us seek alliances that draw us closer to God and support us in our trials.

mots.sens: This term refers to the Ziphites, a group of people living in the region of Ziph. Their name is often associated with treachery, as they allied with Saul to betray David. Spiritually, this reminds us that even among those who seem close, there may be hidden intentions seeking to harm God's servants.

This word means 'refuge' or 'stronghold.' It evokes the idea of protection, security, and sanctuary. In the context of David, it emphasizes his vulnerability and need for divine protection in the face of his enemies, which is a recurring theme in the lives of believers seeking refuge in God.

This term refers to a specific hill, which is an important geographical location in the narrative. As a landmark, it symbolizes the challenges David must overcome. Theologically, it reminds us that believers often face 'hills' or obstacles in their faith journey.

19.epoque: This passage takes place during the period of the united monarchy in Israel, when Saul is king and David is on the run, seeking to escape Saul's jealousy.
19.passage: In this chapter, David is pursued by Saul, who seeks to kill him. The Ziphites, instead of protecting David, betray him by revealing his hiding place to Saul, illustrating the tensions between loyalty and betrayal.
19.culture: In the Israelite culture of the time, loyalty and honor were fundamental values. The betrayal of the Ziphites toward David highlights the danger of fragile alliances and false friends.
19.interpretation: This verse highlights the reality of the persecution and betrayal that David endures. It reminds us that even in moments of vulnerability, God is our refuge and strength, and that the intentions of men cannot nullify divine promises.
19.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of remaining steadfast in our faith, even when those around us seem to betray us. Like David, we can turn to God to find our refuge and strength. In times of crisis, let us remember that our true security lies in Him, not in men.

mots.sens: This word means 'king' and refers to authority, power, and sovereignty. It is often used in the context of divine governance, emphasizing that God is the supreme king and that human kings must act according to His will. In this verse, the use of the term 'king' highlights Saul's desire to control and dominate, while reminding us that true royalty belongs to God.

This term translates as 'soul' and refers to the inner being, life, or essence of a person. It evokes deep desires and human emotions. In the context of this verse, it underscores the intensity of Saul's desire, revealing the inner struggle and motivations that drive him to pursue David, reminding us of the importance of our own spiritual desires and their alignment with divine will.

This verb means 'to deliver' or 'to hand over' and implies an action of transferring responsibility or control. It is often used in a context of submission or devotion. In this verse, it emphasizes the willingness of those who speak to hand David over to Saul, raising questions about loyalty and betrayal, as well as how we entrust our lives into God's hands.

20.epoque: This passage takes place during the transitional period between Saul's reign and David's establishment as king of Israel, a time marked by internal conflicts and struggles for power.
20.passage: In this chapter, David is fleeing from Saul, who seeks to kill him. The men of Keilah, the city where David has taken refuge, find themselves caught between their loyalty to David and the threat posed by Saul.
20.culture: The Israelite culture of the time valued loyalty and faithfulness to the king, but also to God. Political decisions were often influenced by spiritual and ethical considerations.
20.interpretation: This verse illustrates the conflict between human desire for power and divine will. Saul's demand to deliver David reveals his obsession and inability to recognize God's plan for David, who is destined to become the king of Israel.
20.commentaire: This passage reminds us of the importance of discerning between our personal desires and God's will. It urges us to entrust our lives into His hands, even when we face pressures or conflicts. As Christians, we must seek to align our desires with those of God, knowing that He has a perfect plan for each of us.

mots.sens: This word refers to kindness, mercy, or faithfulness toward others. It is often used to describe the unconditional love and grace that God shows to His people. In this verse, 'ḥesed' emphasizes the compassion that people have for Saul, reflecting an aspect of the divine nature that calls for mercy and solidarity.

This term means to bless or praise, and implies an action of giving thanks or conferring divine favor. In the context of this verse, it highlights Saul's desire to receive God's blessing upon those who show him compassion, illustrating the importance of blessing in human and spiritual relationships.

21.epoque: This verse takes place during the period of the Israelite monarchy, as Saul, the first king of Israel, is beset by internal troubles and the threat of David, his designated successor.
21.passage: In this chapter, David is fleeing to escape Saul, who is pursuing him. This verse illustrates a moment where Saul acknowledges the kindness of the men who show him pity, despite the tension and rivalry that exists between him and David.
21.culture: In Israelite culture, the notion of pity and compassion was highly valued, reflecting the values of solidarity and mutual support within the community. Blessings were also considered essential elements in interpersonal relationships.
21.interpretation: This verse highlights the fragility of the human condition, even for a king. Saul's recognition of the goodness of others underscores the importance of mercy and compassion, even in difficult and conflicting circumstances.
21.commentaire: This passage reminds us that even those in positions of power can experience moments of vulnerability. It encourages us to practice compassion and mercy toward others, as these attitudes reflect the character of God. As Christians, we are called to bless those around us, even in times of conflict, and to seek peace and reconciliation.

mots.sens: This term means 'wicked' or 'evil-doer'. It is often used to describe a person who acts immorally or violates divine laws. In the context of this verse, it highlights the cunning and malice of David, who must be watched carefully. It reminds us that evil can hide behind deceptive appearances, and vigilance is necessary in our spiritual walk.

This word means 'to find' or 'to discover'. It implies an active search and a quest for truth. In this verse, it emphasizes the importance of investigation to locate David, shedding light on the need to discern the intentions and actions of others. Spiritually, it invites us to seek the truth in our lives and not to settle for appearances.

This term means 'to observe' or 'to look closely'. It implies deep contemplation and attention to detail. In this context, it underscores the importance of paying attention to signs and indications that may reveal the truth about David's actions. It teaches us to be attentive and to discern God's movements in our lives.

22.epoque: This passage takes place during the period of the monarchy in Israel, while David was fleeing from Saul, who sought to kill him. It is a time of political tensions and personal conflicts, where loyalty and cunning were crucial elements in human relationships.
22.passage: In this chapter, David is on the run and must navigate the dangers surrounding him. This verse shows the anxiety and concern of Saul's men, who seek to locate David due to his growing reputation and his ability to evade their plans.
22.culture: The culture of the time valued cunning and military strategy. Kings and their men often had to demonstrate prudence and intelligence to maintain their power and security. The search for information was essential in a context where alliances and betrayals were common.
22.interpretation: This verse highlights David's cunning and ability to escape his pursuers. Spiritually, it reminds us that even in the most difficult situations, God can give us the wisdom and strategy needed to overcome our challenges. Vigilance and the search for truth are essential in our walk with God.
22.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of prudence and vigilance in our spiritual life. Like David, we face adversities and cunning that seek to divert us from our path. By actively seeking the truth and remaining attentive to God's signs, we can navigate wisely through life's trials. Let us therefore be seekers of truth, ready to discern God's plans and act with discernment.

mots.sens: This term designates a place of refuge or hiding. It evokes the idea of protection and safety, often used to describe places where one hides to escape danger. In the context of David's flight, it underscores David's vulnerability before Saul and the necessity of finding safe places. Spiritually, it can symbolize the search for refuge in God during times of distress.

This verb means 'to know' or 'to be acquainted with', implying a deep and intimate knowledge. In this verse, it is used to express the need to know precisely the places where David is hiding. It emphasizes the importance of knowledge and understanding in the quest for truth. Theologically, it reminds us that God desires for us to know Him and to understand His ways.

This verb means 'to come' or 'to go'. In the context of this verse, it indicates the movement and action of going to the hiding places. It can symbolize the commitment and determination to pursue what is right. Spiritually, it reminds us that our faith must be accompanied by concrete actions to follow God's will.

23.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of Saul, while David is fleeing, seeking to escape Saul's attempts to kill him.
23.passage: In 1 Samuel 23, David receives information about the Philistines attacking Keilah. He consults God to know whether he should intervene, and then he must also face the threat of Saul, who is actively searching for him.
23.culture: At this time, knowledge of territories and refuges was crucial for survival. Alliances and information were often exchanged to locate enemies or allies.
23.interpretation: This verse shows Saul's determination to find David, thus highlighting the tension between the king and the one anointed to succeed him. Spiritually, it reminds us that even in our moments of flight or danger, God knows our places of refuge and guides us.
23.commentaire: In our daily lives, we may find ourselves in situations where we need to seek refuge and safety. Like David, we must be attentive to God's direction and to the knowledge of His ways. This verse encourages us to actively seek the truth and to engage in action to follow divine will, knowing that God is our true refuge.

mots.sens: The word 'Ziph' designates a geographical location, a city situated in the territory of Judah. Its name is often associated with the idea of 'desert' or 'aridity', which can symbolize the trials and challenges that David had to face. Spiritually, Ziph represents the places of refuge that God prepares for His elect, even amid distress.

The term 'midbar' means 'desert' or 'arid land'. In the Bible, the desert is often a place of preparation, purification, and encounter with God. It also evokes dependence on God, as it is in these difficult places that one learns to trust in His provision and protection.

The word 'Maon' refers to another place in the desert, often associated with shelters or refuges. It symbolizes divine protection and God's providence, even when circumstances seem desperate. Spiritually, Maon can be seen as a reminder that God provides safe places for His servants amid dangers.

24.epoque: This passage takes place during the period of the united monarchy of Israel, while David is fleeing from Saul, who seeks to kill him. It is a time of political tensions and internal conflicts within the people of Israel.
24.passage: In this chapter, David is pursued by Saul, and he seeks refuge in the desert. This verse highlights David's strategy to escape Saul and shows the determination of his pursuers to locate him, even in isolated places.
24.culture: In the Israelite culture of the time, the desert was perceived both as a place of danger and divine encounter. Movement in these arid regions required great trust in God for protection and provision.
24.interpretation: This verse illustrates the tension between persecution and divine protection. Despite Saul's threats, David continues to move and seek places of refuge, thus demonstrating his faith in God's providence. It reminds believers that even in the darkest moments, God is present and watches over those who trust Him.
24.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of faith and perseverance in trials. Like David, we sometimes face difficult situations where we must seek God's direction. It is essential to remember that God is our refuge, even in the deserts of our lives, and that He provides for our needs according to His riches and glory.

mots.sens: This term refers to movement, agitation, or pursuit. It evokes the idea of searching or pursuing with determination. In the context of this verse, it emphasizes the intensity of Saul's quest for David, also representing the spiritual struggle that believers may experience in the face of opposition and persecution.

This word means 'refuge' or 'shelter.' It is often associated with a place of safety. In this passage, the wilderness of Maon becomes a space where David seeks to hide, symbolizing the divine protection that God grants to those who trust Him even amid dangers.

This verb means 'to descend.' It can also evoke humility or lowering oneself. In the context of David, descending from the rock may symbolize a humble response to the threat, illustrating how believers sometimes must withdraw to escape persecution while remaining faithful to their mission.

This term refers to a generation or a group of people. In this passage, it can be interpreted as a reference to the community surrounding Saul and David. It reminds us that spiritual conflicts and struggles do not occur only at an individual level but also affect entire groups and generations.

25.epoque: This narrative takes place during the time of the Israelite monarchy, during the reign of Saul, while David is on the run after being anointed as king by Samuel.
25.passage: This verse is found in a context where David is constantly pursued by Saul, who sees him as a threat to his throne. The chapter highlights the tension between David, who is fleeing, and Saul, who seeks to capture him.
25.culture: In the Israelite culture of the time, deserts were often perceived as places of refuge or trial. The dynamic between the king and the fugitive was also significant, illustrating the struggles for power and political tensions.
25.interpretation: This passage illustrates the reality of persecution and the search for refuge. Spiritually, it reminds believers that even in moments of danger, God is present and offers shelter to those who trust in Him.
25.commentaire: This verse teaches us the importance of trusting in God during times of crisis. Like David, we may find ourselves in difficult situations, but we must remember that God is our refuge. By remaining faithful and seeking His presence, we can overcome trials and persecutions.

mots.sens: This word means 'to reign' or 'to be king.' It is often used in the context of authority and power, and can also refer to divine sovereignty. In this verse, it evokes the struggle for power between Saul, the reigning king, and David, the man chosen by God to reign. This highlights the tension between human authority and divine will.

This term means 'to surround' or 'to tighten.' It is used to describe a situation of oppression or imminent danger. In the context of this verse, it illustrates the threat that Saul poses to David, symbolizing the trials that believers may encounter when following God's plan. It also reminds us that even in difficult moments, God is present to protect His faithful ones.

This word means 'to flee' or 'to escape.' It expresses the idea of quickly withdrawing from a dangerous situation. In this passage, it shows David's vulnerability before Saul and the necessity of seeking refuge in God. This underscores the importance of divine dependence in times of crisis.

26.epoque: This passage takes place during the reign of Saul, while David is fleeing due to the king's jealousy. It is a transitional period where God is preparing David to become the king of Israel.
26.passage: In this chapter, David is pursued by Saul who seeks to kill him. This verse shows the critical moment when David is surrounded, representing a desperate situation but highlighting divine protection.
26.culture: In the Israelite culture of the time, the king had absolute power and the loyalty of his subjects was paramount. The struggle between David and Saul illustrates the challenges of kingship and how God chooses His leaders.
26.interpretation: This verse illustrates the tension between God's will and human actions. David, although on the run, is at the center of God's divine plan, while Saul, despite his authority, is in opposition to God. This reminds believers that even in moments of danger, God has a plan and watches over those who trust Him.
26.commentaire: This passage teaches us that even when we feel cornered by circumstances, God is always at work to protect us. Like David, we must learn to flee to the Lord in our trials, knowing that He is in control of our destiny. This encourages us to remain faithful and trust in God, even when the situation seems desperate.

mots.sens: This term means 'messenger' or 'one sent.' It comes from the root 'שָׁלַח' (shalach), which means 'to send.' In the context of this verse, the messenger plays a crucial role in bringing urgent news that prompts Saul to act quickly. Spiritually, this reminds us of the importance of divine communication and the messages that God sends to His people to guide them in critical moments.

The Philistines were a neighboring people and often antagonistic to Israel, symbolizing opposition to God's work. Their invasion represents a direct threat to Israel's security, but also a challenge to the faith of the people. Theologically, this underscores the reality of spiritual struggles that believers encounter, where external forces seek to disrupt God's peace and mission.

The word 'hurry' implies urgency and the necessity to act quickly. This underscores the importance of responsiveness in the face of crises. Spiritually, it teaches us that in our walk with God, there are moments when we must respond quickly to His call, without hesitation, to face the challenges that arise.

27.epoque: This passage takes place during the period of the Israelite monarchy, where Saul is king and faces external threats, notably invasions from the Philistines.
27.passage: In this chapter, David is fleeing to escape Saul, who seeks to kill him. Verse 27 marks a turning point where urgent news from the outside forces Saul to abandon his pursuit of David to confront an immediate threat.
27.culture: In ancient culture, messengers played an essential role in the transmission of information. Their arrival could change the course of events, as here where news of an invasion requires a swift response.
27.interpretation: This verse illustrates how external events can interfere with our plans. Spiritually, it reminds us that even amid our personal struggles, God can use circumstances to divert us from destruction and remind us of our dependence on Him.
27.commentaire: This passage teaches us the importance of staying attentive to the signs and messages that God sends us, even in difficult times. Just as Saul had to react quickly to the threat of the Philistines, we too must be ready to act according to divine direction. This encourages us to be vigilant in our spiritual lives and not to ignore God's calls, especially when challenges arise.

mots.sens: This term literally means 'the rock of divisions' or 'the rock of dispute.' It evokes a place where conflicts have been resolved or where important decisions have been made. Spiritually, it can symbolize the moment when God intervenes to put an end to the enemy's pursuits, thus offering refuge and peace to those who trust Him.

This verb means 'to turn away' or 'to change direction.' In this context, it highlights Saul's change of attitude, as he ceases to pursue David to turn toward another enemy. This shows how God can change the course of events and divert threats against His servants.

This term refers to the Philistines, a people often in conflict with Israel. Their presence reminds us of the spiritual struggles that believers encounter in their lives. In this verse, Saul's return to the Philistines can symbolize the fact that God's enemies are always present, but God protects those who are faithful to Him.

28.epoque: This passage takes place during a time of great tension between Israel and the Philistines, while David is fleeing from Saul, the king of Israel. It is a period of internal and external conflict for the people of Israel.
28.passage: In this chapter, David is constantly in danger due to Saul's jealousy, who seeks to kill him. Verse 28 marks a turning point where Saul abandons his quest to focus on an external threat, highlighting divine intervention in David's life.
28.culture: The name of the place, Séla-Hammachlekoth, reflects the importance of locations in Hebrew culture, often associated with significant events. Place names carry deep meanings and are often linked to historical or spiritual narratives.
28.interpretation: This verse illustrates how God can intervene to divert threats against His servants. Saul's cessation of pursuit symbolizes divine protection and a change of direction in David's life, which is an example of how God guides and preserves those who are faithful to Him.
28.commentaire: This passage reminds us that, even in times of great adversity, God has the power to change the course of events. Like David, we can rest on the promise that God is our refuge and our protector. It is essential to remain faithful and trust in God, for He knows the best path for us, even when circumstances seem dark.
